meta.title: Why Operation Market Garden Was COMPLETELY Avoidable

scenes.beat: A little after seven on 20 Sept 1944, four British tanks cross the Nijmegen road bridge
tanks roll north across the bridge
earlier: American paratroopers rowing across the Waal in canvas boats
under fire in broad daylight
11 km up the road at Arnhem a few hundred British paratroopers still holding
holding for three days, waiting for exactly these tanks
the tanks stopped in the next village, Lent
that night the men at Arnhem lost their bridge

elements.text: THE GERMAN GENERAL FACING THOSE TANKS

scenes.beat: decades later the German general who had faced the four tanks was asked

elements.text:
"THE FOUR TANKS MADE A MISTAKE
WHEN THEY STAYED IN LENT."

"IF THEY HAD CARRIED ON, IT WOULD
HAVE BEEN ALL OVER FOR US."

scenes.beat: his quote: it would have been all over for us
HOST: that's an old man remembering
his artillery map shows almost nothing between Lent and Arnhem
everybody who survived had an explanation
Montgomery blamed the weather
Brereton blamed the slow British tanks
others blamed a traitor, or photographs nobody wanted to look at
a German army that was supposed to be finished and somehow wasn't
Montgomery called the operation 90% successful
HOST: here's tonight's question
not the war in the West, not the advance into Holland

elements.text: THE DEFEAT AT THE LAST BRIDGE

scenes.beat: the defeat at the last bridge
AIDE: Sir, it's one road. How many ways can you get lost? HOST: on this road?
let's count: every turn-off gets assigned; five bridges, two armies, one road

elements.title: THE RULES
lines: 3. A PERSON WHO COULD TAKE IT

scenes.beat: rules: date, place, person; hindsight doesn't count
the Allies get a column, so do the Germans

elements.text: THE PLAN RAN ON A TIMETABLE

scenes.beat: the dispatcher keeps the clock
timetable says tanks reach Arnhem in two to three days
clock starts on a Sunday; one sign we won't paint at all

scenes.chapter: The Summer That Made It Look Easy
scenes.beat: start with the summer that made it look easy
August 1944 the German army in France fell apart
breakout from Normandy, Falaise pocket, chase across France and Belgium
nearly 200,000 missing or captured
British tanks roll into Antwerp, docks almost intact

elements.text: ALLIED HQ: SOMETHING CLOSE TO A FEVER

scenes.beat: the mood was something close to a fever
SHAEF counted 48 divisions worth about 20 infantry and 4 armoured
British airborne staff: the whole Netherlands held no more than 50–100 tanks
the British airborne division admitted what it had assumed
one problem, the oldest one in war: fuel

elements.text: HUNDREDS OF KM FROM THE FRONT

scenes.beat: the petrol was in Normandy and there weren't enough trucks
the Scheldt estuary was still held by the Germans on both banks
a port you can't sail into is a very large car park
Cunningham warned Antwerp would be as much use as Timbuktu
the German 15th Army was quietly escaping across the estuary behind them

elements.text: 5–21 SEPT · GUNS AND TRUCKS · ANYTHING THAT FLOATED

scenes.beat: 65,000 men got across with hundreds of guns and trucks
on the Albert Canal Kurt Chill simply stopped
he grabbed every straggler: sailors, airmen, occupation officials
within hours something like a front line; it only needed to exist
the Allied argument: where to spend the last of the petrol

elements.text: MONTGOMERY: ONE THRUST IN THE NORTH

scenes.beat: broad front vs one thrust through Holland round the West Wall into the Ruhr
sitting in England, unused, the perfect tool; 18 different airborne operations
every one cancelled; ground troops overran the objective
Washington wanted to see what a big airborne army could do
the paratroopers wanted to fight

elements.text: A TOOL LOOKING FOR A JOB

scenes.beat: the tool was looking for a job
AIDE: why does Antwerp get a sign? we haven't started driving
HOST: the cheapest way to lose at Arnhem is to go to Arnhem; first exit isn't on the road

elements.text: PEOPLE SAID SO AT THE TIME

scenes.beat: which exit? Antwerp first: clear the Scheldt in September and there's no Market Garden. That's one
Allied column
10 Sept Montgomery meets Eisenhower inside the Supreme Commander's plane
Montgomery tore up Eisenhower's messages and demanded priority
so fierce Eisenhower had to stop him
by the end Eisenhower had approved the plan
Comet cancelled the same day, reborn bigger with a new name
Market for the airborne part, Garden for the tanks
priority, but only limited priority
Montgomery wrote back: without full priority not before the 23rd, maybe the 26th

elements.title: MONTGOMERY, 11 SEPTEMBER 1944
lines: "THIS DELAY WILL GIVE THE ENEMY TIME

scenes.beat: the sentence worth keeping
Eisenhower's chief of staff promises 1,000 tons a day; Montgomery delighted
pulled the date forward to Sunday the 17th
seven days to plan the largest airborne operation; earlier ones took weeks
AIDE: is that an exit, sir? take more time? HOST: hmm

elements.text: EVERY DAY YOU PLAN = A DAY THEY DIG

scenes.beat: every day spent planning is a day the Germans spend digging
that's a toll either way; no sign

elements.text: ONE ROAD NORTH FROM THE BELGIAN BORDER

scenes.beat: three and a half airborne divisions along a single road
101st at Eindhoven, 82nd at Grave and Nijmegen, British 1st + Poles at Arnhem
then XXX Corps' tanks drive up that road across the carpet, cross the Rhine, keep going

elements.text: THE ROAD: RAISED LIKE A CAUSEWAY

scenes.beat: it really was one road: polder, ditches, dykes; tanks that left it sank
Horrocks: 20,000 vehicles up that road in 60 hours

elements.text:
"HOW MANY DAYS' RATIONS
WILL THEY JUMP WITH?"

scenes.beat: in private Horrocks asked how many days' rations, how long can they hold

elements.text: PLANES FOR ONLY HALF AT ONCE

scenes.beat: only enough planes to carry about half the airborne troops at once

elements.text: DIVISION COMMANDERS: 2 LIFTS ON DAY ONE

scenes.beat: division commanders asked for two flights on the first day
troop carrier commanders refused: no time for repairs, exhausted crews
Brereton sided with the airmen: one lift a day, four days
for the British at Arnhem the decision was multiplied by geography
Urquhart wanted landing zones close to the bridge

elements.text:
SOUTH BANK: TOO SOFT,
CUT UP BY DYKES

scenes.beat: the city full of AA guns; south bank too soft and cut up by dykes
the drop zones went in heathland west of Arnhem, up to 13 km from the bridge
half the half that landed first had to stay and guard the fields

elements.text: DAY ONE: ONE BRIGADE WALKS TO THE BRIDGE

scenes.beat: on day one, one brigade would walk to the bridge

elements.text:
"MY SET REACHES ~5 KM.
THE BRIDGE IS 13 AWAY."

scenes.beat: AIDE: my set reaches about 5 km, the bridge is 13 away. HOST: noted
the Type 22 set: effective range about 5 km
remember that radio, it keeps coming back
which exits? two, both in England: one lift a day, distant drop zones. That's three

entries.label: A2 Two lifts on day one

scenes.beat: Allied column: three

elements.text: THE GERMANS WERE MAKING PLANS TOO

scenes.beat: cross to the other side of the road
3 Sept, a week before Market Garden existed, Model makes a routine decision

elements.text: BATTERED · SENT TO REST AND REFIT

scenes.beat: two battered SS panzer divisions sent near Arnhem to rest and refit
two days later the corps HQ under Bittrich joins them
famous names, shadows of themselves

elements.text: THE WHOLE CORPS · A FRACTION OF PROPER STRENGTH

scenes.beat: the whole corps perhaps six or seven thousand men
some units already packing to leave for Germany

elements.text: KEEP AN EYE ON THAT HOTEL

scenes.beat: Model set up his HQ in a pleasant hotel in Oosterbeek
Model's intelligence officer warned every day of a British offensive

elements.text: ON THE GROUND: ALMOST EXACTLY RIGHT
AIRBORNE: WRONG PLACE (EAST OF THE RHINE)

scenes.beat: right about the ground attack, wrong about the airborne army

elements.text: A SEABORNE INVASION OF NORTHERN HOLLAND?

scenes.beat: Model became convinced a seaborne invasion of northern Holland was coming
even as the transport planes were in the air on the 17th

elements.text: STUDY: LANDINGS ON THE DUTCH COAST

scenes.beat: the German C-in-C West was ordering a study of possible landings on the Dutch coast
which brings us to the first myth on this road
after the war Oreste Pinto claimed Market Garden had been betrayed
Lindemans, 'King Kong', supposedly told the Germans the plan

elements.text: THE BETRAYAL DOESN'T FIT THE TIMETABLE

scenes.beat: AIDE: a traitor? HOST: the traitor might be real; the betrayal doesn't fit the timetable

elements.text: ARRESTED OCTOBER 1944 · DIED IN HIS CELL 1946

scenes.beat: Lindemans arrested 1944, killed himself 1946; a historian concluded he was a double agent

elements.text: A WEEK BEFORE THE PLAN EXISTED

scenes.beat: the SS divisions were ordered to Arnhem a week before the plan existed
the Germans were surprised; that morning they were looking at the coast
a Dutch commission questioned Pinto under oath; he couldn't back it up
the American official history calls the betrayal theory baseless
the panzers at Arnhem weren't a leak; bad luck and good German housekeeping
if you're enjoying the drive, a like helps; unlike the British radios it reaches somebody
bad luck somebody warns you about is another; the Allies were warned

elements.text: 10 SEPTEMBER — THE DAY THE PLAN WAS APPROVED

scenes.beat: by the 10th British intelligence passed on Dutch resistance reports of panzers refitting
SHAEF named the 9th SS and probably the 10th, refitting near Kleve
it worried Bedell Smith enough to go to Montgomery with a warning

elements.text: OR MOVE A US DIVISION NORTH

scenes.beat: drop the equivalent of a second division at Arnhem, or move an American division north

elements.text:
"MONTGOMERY RIDICULED THE IDEA
AND WAVED MY OBJECTIONS ASIDE"

scenes.beat: Montgomery ridiculed the idea and waved his objections aside
the 82nd's intelligence officer noted a captured document on gathering stragglers
fighting capacity seems unimpaired

elements.title: GAVIN'S DIARY
lines: IF I GET THROUGH THIS ONE,

scenes.beat: Gavin's diary: it looks very rough; if I get through this one I will be very lucky

elements.name: Maj Brian Urquhart
elements.role: I Airborne Corps intelligence — no relation to the general

scenes.beat: Major Brian Urquhart kept hearing of German armour; asked for recon flights
12 Sept a photo-recon Spitfire came back with pictures of tanks
pictures that showed tanks near Arnhem
Urquhart took them to his commander, Browning
Browning was dismissive; Urquhart was sent home on sick leave
the story everyone knows; let's check the second myth

elements.text: PICTURES DO. COUNT WHAT COULD DRIVE.

scenes.beat: AIDE: the pictures had tanks. HOST: pictures do; let's count what could drive

elements.text: MOST SS ARMOUR WAS LEFT IN NORMANDY

scenes.beat: barely any: two working Panthers, 5–14 Panzer IVs
on the first day not one German tank went into action against the British
the photographs were weak evidence; the conclusion was right

elements.text: A SHORT MARCH FROM THE DROP ZONES

scenes.beat: the danger was thousands of experienced SS soldiers a short march from the drop zones

elements.text: BEDELL SMITH'S: PUT MORE STRENGTH AT ARNHEM

scenes.beat: which exit? Bedell Smith's: more strength at Arnhem, waved away. That's four
evening of 16 Sept, forecast good, the final decision: go
well over a thousand Allied bombers and fighters hammered flak and airfields
one raid cratered an Me 262 base so none could take off
Sunday 17 September, one o'clock: the clock starts now
about 1,500 transports and nearly 500 gliders took off
weather close to perfect; ready to lose 30%, they lost under three

elements.text: IN ABOUT 80 MINUTES · MOSTLY ON THEIR MARKS

scenes.beat: about 20,000 British and American soldiers landed in 80 minutes
all three divisions called it the best drop they had ever made

elements.text: A SHORT DRIVE FROM HIS HQ

scenes.beat: a few kilometres from the landing zones, at the hotel, Model
Model and his staff packed up and left in a hurry: his own narrow escape struck him first
within hours Model and Bittrich sent the SS toward Arnhem and Nijmegen

elements.text: LANDED NEXT TO THE ONE MAN BEST PLACED TO STOP THEM

scenes.beat: they had landed next to the one man best placed to stop them

elements.text: CAMPED IN THE WOODS RIGHT BESIDE THE LANDING ZONES

scenes.beat: an SS training battalion under Sepp Krafft happened to be camped beside the landing zones

elements.text: 2 OF 3 BATTALIONS RAN STRAIGHT INTO IT

scenes.beat: two of the three British battalions ran straight into it

elements.text: SWALLOWED BY THE TREES AND THE DISTANCES

scenes.beat: the radios gave out almost at once

elements.text: COULDN'T REACH HIS BRIGADES — WENT TO FIND THEM

scenes.beat: Urquhart couldn't reach his brigades, so he went forward himself

elements.suffix: DAYS CUT OFF FROM HIS HQ

scenes.beat: caught in street fighting, hid from patrols, couldn't get back for two days
the third battalion under John Frost took a quiet road along the river
and slipped past
about 740 men reached the north end; at dusk a German armoured column drove south across it

elements.text: HEADING FOR NIJMEGEN · REMEMBER THAT COLUMN

scenes.beat: Gräbner's reconnaissance battalion heading for Nijmegen; remember that column
as the 101st reached the canal bridge at Son, the Germans blew it
almost in their faces
engineers put up a Bailey bridge; tanks only across early on the 19th
the 82nd had a better afternoon: at Grave a platoon took the great bridge over the Maas intact
it had been prepared for demolition; nobody knew why it was never blown

elements.text: BUT AT NIJMEGEN THE PLAN WENT SIDEWAYS

scenes.beat: but at Nijmegen the plan went sideways
Gavin's first worry: the high ground by the border; reports of armour massing in the Reichswald
those reports were false, Dutch civilians soon told the Americans

elements.text:
GAVIN REMEMBERED:
"A BATTALION FOR THE BRIDGE
WITHOUT DELAY"

LINDQUIST REMEMBERED:
"SECURE YOUR OTHER
OBJECTIVES FIRST"

scenes.beat: Gavin's orders remembered two ways: bridge without delay vs other objectives first

elements.text: THE BATTALION WENT TO THE OTHER OBJECTIVES

scenes.beat: only as darkness came did Gavin order: delay not a second longer
hours earlier only a dozen guards; then SS reinforcements arriving from the north; the attack failed

elements.text: GRÄBNER TURNS BACK NORTH — TO CLEAR THE BRIDGE

scenes.beat: Monday morning Gräbner drove back north to clear Frost's men off the bridge
the paratroopers waited in the houses: 12 of 22 vehicles knocked out, Gräbner killed
in England the second lift was running hours late

elements.text: ALLIED: NIJMEGEN BRIDGE ON DAY ONE
GERMAN: GRAVE, READY TO BLOW, LEFT STANDING

scenes.beat: exits: Nijmegen bridge day one (five); Grave left standing (German one)

elements.text: PLAN: WELL ON THE WAY TO ARNHEM

scenes.beat: Monday night: the tanks only just past Eindhoven, running late

elements.text: GRENADIER GUARDS MEET THE 82ND AT GRAVE

scenes.beat: 8:20 Tuesday the Guards meet the paratroopers at Grave

elements.text: NIJMEGEN · THE BIGGEST BRIDGE ON THE ROAD

scenes.beat: by afternoon in Nijmegen staring at the huge steel arch; attacks on the south end failed
about 500 good SS troops dug in

elements.text: A DETAIL THAT TIES THE WHOLE ROAD TOGETHER

scenes.beat: Nijmegen reinforced from Arnhem, but not over the bridge Frost held: by ferry further east

elements.text: EVERY HOUR FROST HELD = AN HOUR NIJMEGEN DIDN'T GET

scenes.beat: every hour Frost held on was an hour the Germans at Nijmegen didn't get
so Gavin came up with a plan that sounded mad
take the bridge from both ends: the 504th crosses in boats and hits the north end

elements.text: THE BOATS: BEHIND THE TANKS, BEHIND THE TRAFFIC

scenes.beat: AIDE: what boats? HOST: coming up the road behind the tanks, behind the traffic. Noted
the boats arrived early Wednesday afternoon: small, flat, canvas and plywood

elements.text: SEVERAL HUNDRED METRES OF FAST RIVER

scenes.beat: about three o'clock the first wave of Cook's battalion pushed off

elements.text: ONLY ~HALF THE BOATS MADE IT BACK

scenes.beat: the Germans opened fire; bullets ripped through the canvas; half the boats came back

elements.text: ACROSS OPEN GROUND TO THE NORTH ENDS OF BOTH BRIDGES

scenes.beat: the men who reached the north bank fought across open ground to the north ends
at ten past seven British tanks drove across

elements.title: MODEL — ORDER
lines: THE RHINE NOT TO BE DESTROYED

elements.text: IT NEVER WENT UP — PART OF THE REASON:
HE WANTED THEM FOR HIS OWN COUNTER-ATTACK

scenes.beat: it never went up: Model had ordered the bridges not destroyed

elements.text: CHANGED HIS MIND CLOSE TO MIDNIGHT

scenes.beat: he only changed his mind close to midnight, after the Americans held it

elements.text: GAVIN: ATTACK FROM BOTH ENDS AT ONCE
+ DUTCH RESISTANCE KEPT THE DEMOLITION PARTIES UNDER FIRE

scenes.beat: Gavin added two reasons: both ends at once, and the Dutch resistance
almost 35 hours at Nijmegen, on a plan with two to three days to reach Arnhem

elements.text: ONE KILOMETRE NORTH OF THE BRIDGE

scenes.beat: the four tanks reached Lent and stopped

elements.text: DARK · CHAOTIC · NOBODY KNEW WHAT WAS AHEAD

scenes.beat: dark, chaotic, nobody knew what waited; not even the Germans knew how thin their line was

elements.text: BEYOND LENT: THE ROAD ON TOP OF A DYKE
A TANK STANDS OUT AGAINST THE SKY

scenes.beat: beyond Lent the road ran on a dyke where a tank stands out against the sky

elements.text: BADLY WOUNDED BY A MORTAR BOMB

scenes.beat: eleven kilometres away Frost's men were finishing their last day; Frost badly wounded

elements.text: BRIEF TRUCE · THE WOUNDED CARRIED OUT INTO CAPTIVITY

scenes.beat: buildings burning with the wounded inside; under a truce they were carried into captivity

elements.text: FOUGHT ON UNTIL ~10 PM · A FEW HELD INTO THE EARLY HOURS

scenes.beat: from that night the Germans had the Arnhem bridge
they poured tanks and men south and built the screen between Lent and Arnhem
the official history calls that screen the greatest delay of all

elements.text: THE SIGN WE PROMISED NOT TO PAINT

scenes.beat: AIDE: should they have kept going from Lent? HOST: the sign we wouldn't paint

elements.text: THE CASE FOR GOING ON IS STRONG
THE CASE AGAINST IS STRONG TOO

scenes.beat: the case for going on vs the case against
a bridge that was falling as they drove: we'll leave that sign blank; paint it in the comments
Thursday the Guards tried the road in daylight; stalled short of Elst
scenes.letterbox: DRAMATISED — THE ROAD TO ELST, 21 SEPTEMBER

scenes.beat: German attacks cut the corridor to the south; tanks turned back; Hell's Highway

elements.text: TWO DAYS LATE · NOT WHERE PLANNED

scenes.beat: Thursday the Polish brigade finally jumped, two days late, not where it had planned
landing zone changed to the polder near Driel on the south bank
114 transports set out, 41 turned back, about a thousand Poles landed
the ferry they were to use was out of action

elements.text: HOW DO YOU TELL THE POLES WHAT'S HAPPENING?

elements.name: Pte Ernest Archer
elements.role: swam the Rhine with a message

scenes.beat: not by radio: Private Ernest Archer swam the Rhine with a message

elements.text: THE MOST RELIABLE RADIO: A MAN WHO COULD SWIM

scenes.beat: AIDE: further than my set reaches too. HOST: the most reliable radio was a man who could swim
the British squeezed into a pocket around Oosterbeek, the same village as Model's hotel

elements.text: AID POSTS IN THE FRONT LINE
HOUSES CHANGED HANDS MORE THAN ONCE

scenes.beat: aid posts sat in the front line in houses that changed hands

elements.text: SUPPLIES ONTO ZONES THE GERMANS NOW HELD

scenes.beat: resupply planes kept dropping onto landing zones the Germans now held

elements.text: NIGHT OF THE 24TH · THE DORSETS CROSS

scenes.beat: the Dorsets tried to cross: of 315, about 200 ended up prisoners, a handful got through
Horrocks and Browning agreed to bring the survivors back

elements.text: HEAVY RAIN · BOOTS MUFFLED WITH CLOTH

scenes.beat: that night, in heavy rain, boots muffled, they slipped down to the river
engineers ferried them across until daylight
about 2,400 came back; roughly 300 left; nearly 100 killed during the crossing
Urquhart, speaking for his men: we have no regrets
someone had to be blamed, and it wasn't going to be the planners
Montgomery told the head of the British Army the Poles had fought very badly
Browning wrote a long letter attacking Sosabowski
under British pressure he was removed from command; many call it a disgrace
in 2006 the Netherlands honoured the Polish brigade and Sosabowski

elements.text: READ THE ROAD BACK, ONE SIGN AT A TIME

scenes.beat: read the road back: Antwerp, seven days, one lift, drop zones, Bedell Smith, Nijmegen, Grave, Nijmegen standing, Lent

entries.label: A2 Two lifts on day one

scenes.beat: five Allied, two German, one nobody can settle
was Market Garden completely avoidable? here's our verdict

elements.text: — BUT NOT BY ONE HEROIC DECISION

scenes.beat: the defeat was avoidable but not by one heroic decision; no spare time built in

elements.text: ANY ONE OF THESE MIGHT HAVE BEEN ENOUGH

scenes.beat: two lifts, closer drop zones, Bedell Smith's advice, Nijmegen bridge the first evening
the Allies needed only one; they took none
what wasn't anyone's fault was the luck; no traitor put them there
the Germans too made mistakes: two great bridges left standing

elements.text: HISTORIANS DON'T AGREE ON WHERE THE WEIGHT LIES

scenes.beat: to be fair, historians don't agree on where the weight lies

elements.title: US ARMY OFFICIAL HISTORY (1963)
lines: HAD MOVED AS FAST AS HORROCKS HOPED.

scenes.beat: the 1963 American official history: the plan drew little criticism; the ground column was too slow
many later writers blame the plan: the drop zones, the single lift, the radios

elements.text: OTHERS: HOW FAST THE GERMANS RECOVERED

scenes.beat: others stress the German recovery: a crust of stragglers and training battalions in under two weeks

elements.text: LATER, SOMETHING CLOSER TO THE TRUTH

scenes.beat: Montgomery, who called it 90% successful, later admitted something closer to the truth

elements.title: MONTGOMERY, MEMOIRS
lines: "IT WAS A BAD MISTAKE ON MY PART.

scenes.beat: it was a bad mistake on my part; I underestimated the difficulties of opening Antwerp
that famous line, a bridge too far, usually credited to Browning

elements.text: NOTHING WRITTEN DOWN AT THE TIME

scenes.beat: we couldn't pin it down, so it stays in the glovebox, unsigned

elements.text: + THOUSANDS MORE IN THE GROUND CORPS

scenes.beat: the bill: ~12,000 airborne casualties; British airborne > 7,000; thousands more
a German signal reported ~3,300 casualties; and the Dutch paid
Eindhoven was bombed during the battle; more than 200 killed
Dutch railway workers struck; the occupiers stopped food shipments
in the hunger winter more than 20,000 Dutch civilians starved

elements.text: THE PORT THAT COULD HAVE OPENED IN SEPTEMBER

scenes.beat: Antwerp received its first convoy on 28 November

elements.text:
"MY COUNTRY CAN NEVER AGAIN AFFORD THE
LUXURY OF ANOTHER MONTGOMERY SUCCESS"

scenes.beat: Prince Bernhard: his country could never again afford another Montgomery success

elements.text: SEND THE FOUR TANKS ON — OR HOLD UNTIL MORNING?

scenes.beat: that's our reading of the road; what's yours? at Lent would you have sent the tanks on?

elements.text: WHICH SIGN WOULD YOU HAVE PAINTED?
SUBSCRIBE — ONE LIFT, NO WAITING FOR DAY TWO

scenes.beat: tell us in the comments, and subscribe: it's one lift, no waiting for the second day

elements.text: THE ARNHEM BRIDGE DIDN'T SURVIVE THE WAR

scenes.beat: 7 Oct 1944 American bombers destroyed it
since 1977 it carries the name of the man who held it: the John Frost Bridge

elements.title: DISPATCHER'S LOG — FINAL ENTRY
lines: PLANNED ARRIVAL AT ARNHEM: DAY 2 OR 3

scenes.beat: final entry: planned arrival day two or three; actual arrival never; close the log
